# shift-router

> Stop paying flagship prices for routine turns — and stop handing your hardest turns to a cheap model. A judge weighs each turn and routes by expected cost; multi-model fallback chains keep you running; complex tasks are orchestrated by a Smart CTO that delegates to Fast subagents. Two editions: pi-coding-agent and DeepSeek Harness.

## About

shift-router is a family of task-level model routers — **pi-shift-router** (v1.7.0, pi-coding-agent extension) and **dsh-shift-router** (v0.6.0, DeepSeek Harness plugin). Both classify every turn and route between two roles:

- **Fast = Engineer** — handles the workload: writes code, runs tests, fixes bugs, follows established patterns. For routine, well-defined, low-stakes work.
- **Smart = CTO** — for the work that matters: sets direction, corrects course, reviews results, and takes on the hard problems itself — architecture, design review, security audit, multi-step planning, irrecoverable actions.

**Routing is expected-cost, not vote-counting (v1.4.0+).** A judge reads each turn and returns a tier plus a confidence. That confidence is read as `pSmart` (the chance this turn needs the strong model), and the turn runs Smart iff `pSmart ≥ θ`, where `θ = 1 / reworkPenalty` (default R=3 → θ ≈ 0.33). The bar sits deliberately above 50%: upgrading a routine turn wastes the price difference once, while keeping a hard turn cheap costs a redo plus the smart model anyway plus your time. The rule is price-independent — the price gap cancels out, so the only thing that matters is how badly a wrong call hurts. Below `minConfidence` (0.5) the router **holds position rather than guessing**. Upgrades are immediate; downgrades need `downgradeMemory` (default 2) consecutive decisive fast turns.

**Gear presets (v1.4.0):** `/router eco` (R=2, θ=0.5 — conservative and cheap), `/router default` (R=3, θ≈0.33), `/router sport` (R=5, θ=0.2 — eager, any real chance escalates). Top-level, tab-completable, persisted.

**Three judge modes (v1.7.0):** `fast-chain` (default — reuse the Fast tier chain), `custom` (a dedicated judge chain), `decision` (a decision model such as TypeSafe Jev / System One class, Beta opt-in — returns a typed choice with a probability instead of prose, so there is no JSON parse step and no malformed-reply failure class; ~$0.0001 per turn). Jev is opt-in and labelled Beta because it is currently slow per verdict (1.4–6.6 s while provider capacity ramps) and a September 2026 independent evaluation found decision models behind the best LLM on 14 of 15 annotation tasks; it suits batch and background routing, while interactive turns are still better served by the LLM judge.

**Judge availability ladder (v1.7.0):** judge chain → LLM judge → no routing at all. It covers both a rotted config and call-time failures (429/5xx/timeout) in the same turn, for every mode. The last rung behaves as if the plugin were not installed — no model switch, orchestration cleared, session model restored — and it says so once per session. A failed judge call never fabricates a verdict (v1.4.2 fixed a bug where two consecutive judge outages silently downgraded a Smart session).

**Runtime failover:** on 429/402/5xx — including "Insufficient Balance" / 余额不足 and Codex usage-limit exhaustion — the failing model enters exponential-backoff cooldown (5xx starts at 1m: 1m → 4m → 16m → 1h → 4h… capped 6h; a failover-worthy 4xx starts at 16m) and the next healthy model in the same tier takes over, mid-turn. Auth/config errors (400/401) never trigger failover.

**Task-level orchestration (v1.0.0, hardened through v1.5.0):** when the judge says a task is complex and orchestration is in auto mode (default), the Smart tier runs as a CTO that plans the work, delegates implementation to Fast engineer subagents (fresh context, model pinned from the Fast tier), reviews each result, and iterates until clean. Simple tasks never orchestrate. Hard caps: maxRounds 3, escalationThreshold 2. Every orchestrated turn ends with an **acceptance audit** (v1.3.0): deterministic checks always run (every worker reported back, a CTO summary is present, no silent hard-cap hit), plus an optional fast-tier LLM audit that checks grounding, goal alignment, and delivered quality — findings surface as console.warn + toast and `/router status → Last audit`. Re-delegations must carry a structured failure report (convergence protocol, v1.2.0). Per-worker cost attribution (v1.5.0) shows delegation spend separately (`orchestration $0.0689, 5 workers`) instead of hiding it inside the main-agent figures. Requires pi-subagents; without it, complex tasks run directly on Smart (no crash, no deadlock).

## The family

| | pi-shift-router | dsh-shift-router |
|---|---|---|
| Runtime | pi-coding-agent extension | DeepSeek Harness plugin |
| Version | v1.7.0 | v0.6.0 |
| Install | `pi install npm:pi-shift-router` | `git clone …/dsh-shift-router && npm install && npm run build` + `dsh plugin --profile web add <path>` |
| Config | `/router config` wizard | GUI "Shift-Router" card + `/router config` (get/set/unset/diff) |
| Capabilities | expected-cost routing, three judge modes, judge ladder, cache-aware routing, failover, orchestration, TUI status dashboard | same, plus `/router allow-workers` to pin delegated workers to the Fast chain |
| Tests | 577 unit tests | 424 unit tests + credential-free headless e2e |

## Key facts

- Runtime: Node.js ≥ 24 (pi), Node.js ≥ 22 (DSH)
- Dependencies: pi-shift-router declares one host-provided dependency (`@earendil-works/pi-tui`, bundled by pi); dsh-shift-router has zero runtime dependencies
- License: MIT
- Author: green-dalii
- Repositories: https://github.com/green-dalii/pi-shift-router · https://github.com/green-dalii/dsh-shift-router
- npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/pi-shift-router

## Install (pi)

```bash
pi install npm:pi-shift-router
```

Registers in ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and auto-loads on the next pi launch.

Optional (recommended) for orchestration:

```bash
pi install npm:pi-subagents
```

## Install (DeepSeek Harness)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/green-dalii/dsh-shift-router.git
cd dsh-shift-router
npm install && npm run build
dsh plugin --profile web add /path/to/dsh-shift-router
```

The bundle's cordis.patch.yml inserts the plugin into any profile that lists it. Tier models come from the settings panel or the patch row. Configuration is editable live (GUI panel + `/router config`; code changes still need a restart).

## Configure

Inside pi, run `/router config` and pick one Fast + one Smart model. Save to user or project scope. On DSH, edit the `shift-router` settings namespace in the GUI or via `/router config set`.

## Verify

`/router status` shows the dashboard: your tiers, the last decision and why, the tier chains with inline cooldowns, per-model context and cache gauges, the money section, and which config layer is authoritative. The next turn triggers the first judge call.

## Commands

- `/router status` — open the status dashboard (TUI): live model, last decision, money, chains, health, config layer
- `/router on` / `/router off` — enable / disable routing
- `/router eco|default|sport` — gear presets for the expected-cost bar (persisted, tab-completable)
- `/router config` — launch the configuration wizard (pi) / interactive editor with get/set/unset/diff (DSH)
- `/router quiet` — toggle inline toast notifications
- `/router verbose` — toggle verbose logging (writes to ~/.pi/agent/logs/shift-router.log, never stdout)
- `/router orchestrate auto|off` — task-level orchestration on (default) or plain two-tier routing
- `/router allow-workers on|off` — DSH only: pin delegated workers to your Fast chain
- `/route-force <tier>` — pin Smart or Fast for the next turn
- `/route-force <provider>/<model>` — pin a specific model for the next turn
- `/route-force auto` — clear manual override

`/router stats` was removed in v1.4.0 — use `/router status`, which now shows the gear, R and the effective θ.

`/router status` reports cost telemetry: per-tier spend and a savings baseline — what the session would have cost if every turn ran on your Smart model (i.e. no router). Delegated workers are accounted separately (`orchestration $0.0689, 5 workers`) so the cost of orchestration is never hidden in the main-agent figures.

## Configuration

Two-layer config (pi): user (`~/.pi/agent/pi-shift-router.json`) + project (`<cwd>/.pi/pi-shift-router.json`). Project wins on conflict. On DSH, config lives in the `shift-router` settings namespace (same store for GUI and commands).

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "tiers": {
    "fast":  { "models": [
      { "provider": "deepseek", "model": "deepseek-v4-flash", "priority": 1 },
      { "provider": "kimi",     "model": "kimi-k3",          "priority": 2 }
    ] },
    "smart": { "models": [{ "provider": "kimi", "model": "kimi-k3", "priority": 1 }] }
  },
  "routing": {
    "mode": "auto",
    "judge": { "mode": "fast-chain" },
    "judgeTimeout": 5000,
    "window": { "minConfidence": 0.5 },
    "economics": { "mode": null, "reworkPenalty": 3, "downgradeMemory": 2 },
    "cacheAware": { "enabled": true, "sameFamilyPenalty": 1.5 }
  },
  "orchestration": { "mode": "auto", "maxRounds": 3, "escalationThreshold": 2, "audit": { "enabled": true } },
  "ux": { "quietMode": false, "statusBar": true, "inlineToast": true, "routerLogVerbose": false }
}
```

## FAQ

- **What if I don't configure any models?** Both tiers start empty. The router is a no-op; pi/DSH uses its default model. Run `/router config`.
- **Does the Judge add noticeable latency?** A few thousand tokens at Fast-tier pricing; end-to-end classification typically 200ms–2s. Status bar shows `🧭 judging…`. A decision model removes the parse step but is currently slower per verdict — see the judge modes section.
- **What if my primary model 429s, runs out of credit, or times out?** Exponential-backoff cooldown — 5xx from 1m, failover-worthy 4xx (429/quota, 402 insufficient balance, Codex usage-limit exhaustion) from 16m, capped at 6h; next healthy model in the same tier takes over. A 2xx response clears the cooldown.
- **What happens when the judge is unavailable?** The router walks a ladder: judge chain → LLM judge → no routing at all (behaving as if the plugin were not installed, announced once per session). It never guesses a tier.
- **What is task-level orchestration?** A smart verdict on a complex task makes the Smart tier act as CTO: plan → delegate to Fast subagents → review → iterate → accept, then a post-turn acceptance audit. `/router orchestrate off` disables it. Needs pi-subagents (pi) / a deployment-pinned worker model (DSH, or run `/router allow-workers on`).
- **Are DSH subagents routed?** No — subagents keep their own model; only top-level agents are routed. `/router allow-workers on` writes your Fast chain into the harness subagent allowlist so delegated workers run on Fast.
- **Does this work across different providers?** Yes — each tier is an ordered list of `{provider, model, priority}` pairs.
- **Can I monitor cost?** Yes — `/router status` reports per-tier spend, a savings baseline vs. running everything on Smart, and a separate orchestration line for delegated workers.
